title: actions/checkout fails in container-based jobs on act_runner because Node.js is expected inside the job container
body:
I'm currently a GitHub Actions user and I'm evaluating a migration to Gitea. While comparing the two runners, I found a behavioral difference around how actions/checkout (and JavaScript Actions in general) is executed when a job specifies a container:.

On GitHub Actions, a JavaScript Action like actions/checkout runs on the runner host, using the Node.js runtime bundled with the runner. It does not need Node.js to be present inside the job container. This means a workflow like the following works fine on GitHub, even though the skopeo image contains no Node.js:
```
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    container:
      image: quay.io/containers/skopeo:latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: skopeo --version
```
On Gitea with act_runner, the same workflow fails, reporting that node is missing. This appears to be because act_runner executes JavaScript Actions inside the job container, so the container image must itself provide Node.js.

Expected behavior
It would be ideal if act_runner could handle JavaScript Actions the way GitHub's runner does — by providing a Node.js runtime on the host side (or injecting one into the job container) so that actions/checkout and other JS Actions work regardless of whether the job container ships with Node.js.

Actual behavior
act_runner tries to invoke node inside the job container. If the container image (e.g. quay.io/containers/skopeo:latest) does not include Node.js, the step fails.

Why this matters for migration
This is a notable migration friction point: many users run jobs in minimal, purpose-built container images (tool images like skopeo, kaniko, aws-cli, etc.) that intentionally contain only the tool they need. On GitHub these workflows work because the runner supplies Node for JS Actions. 


I notice that this issue has been reopened. When working with various external images or workflows, there is often no guarantee that `apt install nodejs` will be supported, which can lead to significant time spent modifying `workflow.yml` files. In such cases, invoking the Node.js instance directly from the host machine might be a better approach.
https://gitea.com/orbit/orbit/issues/538
